steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Timber working: tenon saw (straight cuts), coping saw (curves), chisel (paring and mortising), plane (flat surfaces), file/sandpaper (smooth finish). Jointing: PVA glue, screws, dowels, dovetails, mortise-and-tenon.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Metal working: hacksaw (cutting bar/flat stock), pillar drill (accurate holes), file (shaping and deburring), sheet metal snips (cutting thin sheet), tap and die (internal/external threads). Joining: soldering, brazing, welding, rivets, nuts and bolts.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Polymer working: laser cutter (2D profiles from sheet acrylic/MDF), line bender (folds acrylic along a heated element), strip heater, drill (slow speed to avoid melting). Joining: acrylic cement (capillary action), solvent weld (PVC), ultrasonic welding, snap-fit joints.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Workshop safety: tie hair back, no loose clothing, safety goggles for all cutting/drilling, clamp work in a vice, use push sticks on machinery, know emergency stop positions.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Describe how to bend a 3 mm acrylic sheet to create a 90-degree stand using a line bender. | Explain the difference between soldering and brazing, and when each would be used. | State four workshop safety rules when using a pillar drill.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Describe processes step by step in chronological order - marks for sequence accuracy Always include safety precautions when describing workshop processes Know the difference between permanent joints (weld, solder, glue) and non-permanent (screws, bolts, nuts)
